title: Battle of the Bulge (16 Dec 1944 - 25 Jan 1945)

briefing.historical: In the early hours of 16 December 1944 Germany launched its last major offensive in the West through the Ardennes, aiming at the Meuse and the port of Antwerp (B02). Three German armies - Sixth Panzer, Fifth Panzer and Seventh - struck a thinly held, quiet sector. Stubborn defence at Elsenborn Ridge and Bastogne and the arrival of reinforcements broke the timetable; the weather cleared on 23 December, Bastogne was relieved on 26 December and the salient was reduced by late January. Reinforcement arrival points and some arrival days are approximate.
briefing.situation: Germany must break through the American line, seize the road hubs of St. Vith and Bastogne and reach the Meuse before Allied reserves and air power arrive; its fuel is scarce, so capturing American fuel dumps is vital. The Allies must hold the shoulders at Elsenborn and Bastogne, delay the panzers, keep the Meuse crossings at Dinant, Namur and Huy, and then counter-attack. Start positions are approximate sector anchors.

playableNations.summary: Armoured breakthrough with scarce fuel against a thin line that will be reinforced day by day.
Absorb the surprise, hold the shoulders and the hubs, then counter-attack.
Command XXX Corps on the Meuse: a stop-line behind the Americans.

objectives.description: Capture Liège, opening the road to Antwerp (Hitler's objective, B02; Antwerp lies outside this map).

objectives.description: Destroy a third of the German units; the offensive was exhausted by attrition and fuel shortage (B02, B06).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, "Battle of the Bulge order of battle" (German armies/corps/divisions with commanders; US First and Third Army corps/divisions; XXX Corps; air commands). The page states it reflects a point near the end of the campaign, not 16 Dec, so unit presence on 16 Dec relies on other sources where possible.

Wikipedia, "Battle of the Bulge" (timeline: 16 Dec barrage 05:30; 17 Dec Büllingen fuel and Malmedy; 18 Dec Stavelot; 19 Dec Stoumont, Meuse bridges ordered held, 101st at Bastogne; 20 Dec Bastogne cut off, Montgomery commands First/Ninth Armies; 21 Dec St Vith evacuated; 22 Dec ultimatum; 23 Dec weather clears; 24 Dec Foy-Notre-Dame; 26 Dec 16:50 relief; 1 Jan Bodenplatte; 3 Jan counter-offensive; 16 Jan Houffalize; 22 Jan 6th Pz Army cedes sector; 23 Jan St Vith recaptured; 25 Jan end; strengths).

US Army (C. B. MacDonald), "The Ardennes: Battle of the Bulge", Ch. V "The Sixth Panzer Army Attack" (HyperWar): 99th and 2nd Infantry Divisions, 14th Cavalry Group, 38th Cavalry Squadron, 1st Division 26th Infantry, German I SS Panzer Corps / LXVII Corps divisions, Kampfgruppe Peiper route 16-17 Dec.

US Army (MacDonald), "The Ardennes", Ch. XII "The First Attacks at St. Vith" (HyperWar): 106th Infantry Division, CCB 9th Armored, 7th Armored Division arrival 17 Dec, 14th Cavalry Group, 112th Infantry, German LXVI Corps, Fuehrer Begleit Brigade, 116th Panzer, 9th SS Panzer (19 Dec), 82nd and 101st Airborne approach.

US Army (MacDonald), "The Ardennes", Ch. XIX "The Battle of Bastogne" (HyperWar): 101st Airborne (arrived 19 Dec), CCB 10th Armored, CCR 9th Armored destroyed 18-19 Dec, 28th Division remnants, Panzer Lehr, 26th VGD, 2nd Panzer, 15th Panzergrenadier (Christmas Day), 5th Parachute, airdrops 23 Dec, relief 26 Dec.

US Army (MacDonald), "The Ardennes", Ch. III "Troops and Terrain" (HyperWar): German planning debate; start delayed (27 Nov to 16 Dec) by fuel and supply shortages; 4SS panzer divisions and 2nd Panzer held free for the offensive.
Wikipedia, "Siege of Bastogne" (20-26 Dec; 101st Airborne, CCB 10th Armored, Team Desobry at Noville, 705th TD Bn; "NUTS" 22 Dec; 4th Armored relief 26 Dec).
Wikipedia, "Battle of St. Vith" (106th Division new and poorly equipped; ~7,000 surrendered on Schnee Eifel 19 Dec; Clarke withdrew 21 Dec on Montgomery's orders).

Secondary accounts of Peiper at Büllingen (warfarehistorynetwork.com "Adolf Hitler Sends Joachim Peiper to the Bulge"; liberationroute.com "Battle of Büllingen"): fuel dump captured 17 Dec; figures conflict (about 50,000 gallons vs 200,000 litres); larger depot figures near Stavelot/La Gleize (2-3 million gallons) conflict and one account says the Stavelot supplies were destroyed. Uncertain.

Secondary accounts of the weather (ww2gp.org Ardennes pages; US Air Force Mildenhall "A look at air power in the Battle of the Bulge"; DTIC ADA121480 meteorology report): thick overcast, fog and snow 16-22 Dec grounded Allied aircraft; high pressure and clear, much colder weather from 23 Dec; air drops to Bastogne from 23 Dec. No numeric temperatures retrieved.

US Army (MacDonald), "The Ardennes", chapter text on the Meuse screen (as quoted in search snippets of sonsoflibertymuseum.org Ch. 22): XXX Corps (Horrocks) ordered to hold the Meuse as a stop-line; 29th Armoured Brigade refitting in western Belgium ordered to the Namur-Dinant sector; British armoured cars screened Liège-Namur. Only snippet-level retrieval; division list and dates not confirmed.

Wikipedia unit articles: 26th Infantry Division (United States) (moved north to Luxembourg 19-21 Dec 1944); 6th Armored Division (United States) (ordered north of Metz 23 Dec 1944); 87th Infantry Division (United States) (SHAEF reserve 24-28 Dec, committed in Belgium 29 Dec 1944). Arrival areas are not given.

Wikipedia, "Operation Bodenplatte" (1 Jan 1945 targets and Allied units based there: Sint-Truiden A-92 with the 48th and 404th Fighter Groups; Asch Y-29 with the 352nd and 366th Fighter Groups). WEAK for 16 Dec: it documents basing on 1 Jan 1945 only. No Luftwaffe airfield coordinates or Allied strengths given; Luftwaffe JG units omitted.

GAME-SCALE ABSTRACTION (internal): manpower, equipment points, morale/experience/organisation, nation resources and income, objective points and victory thresholds are nominal game values, NOT historical strengths. German fuel scarcity is represented by a reduced game-scale fuel pool and income (sourced qualitatively by B06).
Modern gazetteer coordinates (Wikipedia/GeoNames) rounded to 0.01 deg, recalled by the author; accuracy +/-0.05 deg towns, +/-0.1 deg depots/ridges.

POSITION POLICY (internal): no source gives division start coordinates. Start positions are approximate sector anchors inferred from the named towns/sectors in B03-B05 with a small deterministic spread. Reinforcement arrival times marked approximate where the source gives only the day or only the event.

BORDER POLICY (internal): initialControl polygons are coarse approximations of the 16 Dec 1944 front (all Belgium, Luxembourg and liberated France Allied-held; Germany east of the border incl. West Wall); small US-held pockets inside Germany (e.g. around Monschau) are ignored.
